subject: Streaming & tail latency discovery — envelope + test window
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2024 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming & tail latency discovery — envelope + test window

Hi Samir —

Great to meet today, and thanks for walking us through NovusAI's inference topology. Quick recap and a tight set of asks so we can scope a short performance probe next week: 

1) Traffic envelope: you mentioned most calls are single-turn chat with median token output ~40 and a small subset of streaming long responses (up to ~600 tokens) for summarization. Can you confirm a representative distribution file (sample requests by percentile) or the 3 buckets we discussed (short/medium/long)? If you can drop a small JSON snippet that would be perfect (see requested format in attached "traffic-envelope-sample.json").

2) SLO targets: you said current provider shows p95 ~ 150ms and p99 ~ 450ms for non-streaming; for streaming you observe intermittent tailing spikes. For the hosted comparison we typically align around target envelopes — please confirm the p95/p99 thresholds you need for an apples-to-apples check. 

3) Concurrency & throughput: expected sustained concurrency during peak window and acceptable ramp/fanout pattern (steady vs bursty). If you can provide expected concurrency and requests/sec for the peak 10-minute window, we’ll size the probe.

4) Security/process: do we need an NDA/PO prior to running synthetic traffic? You referenced procurement and SOC docs — please loop in procurement if there are gating items.

Proposed next steps:
- You share traffic envelope JSON + confirmation of target p95/p99 and peak concurrency (Samir) — by EOD Tue if possible.
- Our SRE (Ben) will propose a 2-hour probe window and the exact test harness and metrics we’ll collect.
- We’ll schedule the probe Wed/Thu next week (tentative).

Attached: slo-probe-plan.pdf (sketch of what we’ll collect) and traffic-envelope-sample.json (format).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar hold once we have timing.

— Rachel

From: Samir Patel <samir@novusai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@novusai.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2024 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming & tail latency discovery — envelope + test window

Thanks Rachel — good notes. Quick answers inline: 

- Traffic envelope: attaching a short sample (we'll upload the full sampling file to the Drive link you suggested). Short/Medium/Long split for our production: 70% short (20–60 tokens), 25% medium (60–200), 5% long (200–600 streaming).

- SLOs: Our SLA ask for user-facing chat is p95 <= 200ms end-to-end, p99 <= 600ms. For streaming summarization we need p95 <= 400ms for first-chunk latency and p99 <= 900ms (we understand streaming adds complexity).

- Concurrency: baseline concurrent users 80–120, peak up to 350 for a 5–10 minute burst during batch reports. Typical QPS at peak is ~220.

- Security: procurement will confirm if we need an NDA/PO; I cc'ed procurement. We can run a synthetic window without production keys if you prefer.

I’ll upload the sample traffic by EOD. If you can propose a 2-hour window Wed or Thu that works for engineering.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Engineering, NovusAI
samir@novusai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novusai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2024 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming & tail latency discovery — envelope + test window

Samir, Rachel — thanks for the envelope details. A few technical clarifications so our probe collects comparable metrics: 

1) Payload shape: please confirm average request size in bytes and whether you include long system prompts in a subset of requests. Those increase tokenization overhead.

2) Streaming semantics: are you using server-sent events (SSE) with ~256–1024B chunks, or chunk-per-token? Our streaming latency model differentiates first-chunk latency vs per-chunk intervals — please indicate chunk strategy.

3) Warm vs cold cache: does NovusAI use multi-turn KV caching on the client side or per-request stateless calls? If you have a cache-window we should reproduce (e.g., 1–2 minute conversation sessions).

Proposed probe plan (high-level):
- 2-hour window split into: 30m ramp, 60m steady-peak (simulate 80/25/5% distribution), 30m cooldown.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 end-to-end, server-first-chunk (streaming), per-chunk intervals, CPU/GPU utilization, request queueing time, success/error breakdown.
- Pass criteria (suggested for hosted baseline run): p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 500ms for non-streaming; streaming first-chunk p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 800ms. These are deliberately slightly tighter than your ask so we can show headroom vs incumbent. We can relax to your stated targets for procurement conversations.

Attachments: slo-probe-plan.pdf (detailed probe steps).

If that plan looks good, Rachel — can you propose calendar windows Wed 22nd 10–12 PT or Thu 23rd 14–16 PT? Samir — either works?

— Ben
Ben Carter
SRE — Performance & Reliability, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
